thought_title: Born of David's seed and of the Spirit

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Περίψημα τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα τοῦ σταυροῦ, ὅ ἐστιν σκάνδαλον τοῖς ἀπιστοῦσιν, ἡμῖν δὲ σωτηρία καὶ ζωὴ αἰώνιος, ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ συζητητής; ποῦ καύχησις τῶν λεγομένων συνετῶν; [2] ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐκυοφορήθη ὑπὸ Μαρίας κατ’ οἰκονομίαν θεοῦ ἐκ σπέρματος μὲν Δαυείδ, πνεύματος δὲ ἁγίου: ὃς ἐγεννήθη καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη, ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ.
pass_a_gloss: My spirit is a humble offscouring given for the cross, which is a stumbling block to those who do not believe, but to us it is salvation and eternal life. Where is the wise man? Where is the debater? Where is the boasting of those who are called intelligent? For our God, Jesus the Christ, was carried in the womb by Mary according to God's plan of salvation, from the seed of David on the one hand, but from the Holy Spirit on the other. He was born and was baptized, so that by his suffering he might cleanse the water.

lemmas.gloss: offscouring; in letter formulas, a humble devoted offering of oneself (cf. 1 Cor 4:13)
God; here predicated of Jesus Christ: our God
carry in the womb, be pregnant with
household management; divine plan, ordered arrangement

pass_b_english: My spirit is a lowly offering laid down for the cross. To those who do not believe, the cross is a stumbling block (1 Corinthians 1:23); to us it is salvation and eternal life (1 Corinthians 1:18). Where is the wise man? Where is the debater (1 Corinthians 1:20)? Where is the boasting of the so-called clever?

For our God, Jesus the Christ, was carried in the womb by Mary, as God had planned: of David's seed (Romans 1:3), yet of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:18, 20). He was born, and he was baptized, so that by his suffering he might make the water clean.

choices.english: My spirit is a lowly offering laid down for the cross
choices.why: περίψημα is literally 'offscouring' (1 Cor 4:13) but became a formula of humble self-devotion; Ignatius offers his spirit to the cross. 'Offering' keeps both the lowliness and the devotion.
rejected: counted as nothing (ANF; loses the devotion)
devoted to the cross (drops the lowliness)

choices.term: ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός
choices.why: Ignatius calls Jesus 'our God' outright; the article on Χριστός is kept as 'the Christ'.
rejected: our God Jesus Christ (flattens the article)

choices.why: οἰκονομία is God's ordered plan for salvation. Mary stays the agent of ἐκυοφορήθη ὑπὸ Μαρίας; the plan is a separate 'according to' relation.

choices.english: by his suffering he might make the water clean
choices.why: πάθος is Christ's suffering; the water is cleansed for baptism by it.
rejected: by submitting (reads πάθος as πάσχειν in a weaker sense)

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF 'Let my spirit be counted as nothing for the sake of the cross' loosens περίψημα (an offering of humble devotion, not mere nothingness) and turns an indicative into a wish; 'appointment' is narrow for οἰκονομία.

bible_refs.note: cross as salvation to us versus folly to the perishing; Ignatius's contrast
ποῦ σοφός; ... ποῦ συζητητής; verbal match
σκάνδαλον applied to the crucified Christ
ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου of the conception

notes: Whole chapter 18 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
Possible further echoes kept out of the reading text: Romans 3:27 ('where is boasting?') and 1 Corinthians 1:19 (τῶν συνετῶν).
Ephesians 18:1 in Lake opens without a connective after 17:2; chapter divisions are editorial.

review.notes: Checked p1, both internal sections. Greek «Περίψημα τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα τοῦ σταυροῦ, ὅ ἐστιν σκάνδαλον τοῖς ἀπιστοῦσιν, ἡμῖν δὲ σωτηρία καὶ ζωὴ αἰώνιος» matches Pass A «humble offscouring given for the cross, which is a stumbling block to those who do not believe, but to us it is salvation and eternal life» and Pass B’s cross as stumbling block to unbelievers and salvation and eternal life to us. «ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ συζητητής; ποῦ καύχησις τῶν λεγομένων συνετῶν» is kept as three questions. «ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐκυοφορήθη ὑπὸ Μαρίας» keeps Jesus as our God and Mary as the one who carried him; «ἐκ σπέρματος μὲν Δαυείδ, πνεύματος δὲ ἁγίου» keeps both origins; «ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ» stays purpose, suffering as instrument, water as object. Inline citations agree with the supplied bible_refs and are not false. Title names the David-and-Spirit thought, not only the locus.

Source paragraph 1 matches Ignatius Ephesians 18:1-2 per Lake 1912 Loeb text. Pass A and B both accurately reflect Greek: Περίψημα rendered as 'humble offscouring'/'lowly offering' (lemma justified); σκάνδαλον as 'stumbling block'; σωτηρία and ζωὴ αἰώνιος as 'salvation and eternal life'; interrogatives preserved. Agency: θεὸς ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς as 'our God, Jesus the Christ'; ἐκυοφορήθη ὑπὸ Μαρίας as 'carried in the womb by Mary'; οἰκονομίαν θεοῦ as 'according to God's plan'/'as God had planned'; ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυίδ and ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου as 'from the seed of David... from the Holy Spirit'/'of David's seed... yet of the Holy Spirit'. Modality: ἵνα τῷ πάθει τὸ ὕδωρ καθαρίσῃ as 'so that by his suffering he might cleanse the water'/'so that by his suffering he might make the water clean'. Negation: none in source. Scripture: all inline citations in Pass B correspond to actual parallels noted in bible_refs and notes (1 Cor 1:18, 20, 23; Rom 1:3; Matt 1:18,20) and are correctly added per rule. Title 'Born of David's seed and of the Spirit' names the thought. No omissions, additions, or contradictions. Covered source paragraphs: [1].
